Signing and encrypting for people, in the formats mail and key tools read: text armor, X.509 certificates with CMS and S/MIME, OpenPGP, a store of other people's keys, and keys that stay on a token.

Each section is one help page: what its functions are for, and the example
of the page as it runs. `?name` gives the arguments and the value in full.

## Text armor

`nqarmor()`, `nqdearmor()`: `nqarmor()` writes bytes as text between a `-----BEGIN` and an `-----END` line (RFC 7468), to paste into a message or a web page; `nqdearmor()` reads it back and gives the label with the bytes.

```{r nqarmor}
a <- nqarmor("NOQTIS TEST", as.raw(1:40))
cat(a)
nqdearmor(a)$label
```

## Certificates

`nqcert()`, `nqkemcert()`, `nqcertinfo()`: `nqcert()` writes a self-signed X.509 certificate for a signature key (ML-DSA, SLH-DSA or Ed25519) under a name and an e-mail address; `nqkemcert()` writes the certificate of an ML-KEM key, issued by that signature key, which is what mail is encrypted to; `nqcertinfo()` says what a certificate holds.

```{r nqcert}
k <- nqkeygen("ML-DSA-44")
cert <- nqcert(k$sk, k$pk, "ML-DSA-44", "Ada Example",
  email = "ada@example.org"
)
nqcertinfo(cert)$name
e <- nqkeygen("ML-KEM-768")
kc <- nqkemcert(k$sk, "ML-DSA-44", cert, e$pk, "ML-KEM-768")
nqcertinfo(kc)$kem
```

## CMS and S/MIME messages

`nqcmssign()`, `nqcmsverify()`, `nqcmsencrypt()`, `nqcmsdecrypt()`, `nqsmimesign()`, `nqsmimeverify()`, `nqsmimeencrypt()`, `nqsmimedecrypt()`: the CMS functions sign a message with a certificate and its key, check a signed message against the certificates the caller trusts, and encrypt to the ML-KEM certificates of the recipients; the S/MIME functions do the same with a mail entity and give the mail to send. A signature is good only when its signer's certificate is one of the anchors.

```{r nqcmssign}
k <- nqkeygen("ML-DSA-44")
cert <- nqcert(k$sk, k$pk, "ML-DSA-44", "Ada Example")
s <- nqcmssign(k$sk, cert, charToRaw("hello"), "ML-DSA-44")
v <- nqcmsverify(s, list(cert))
rawToChar(v$content)
v$signer$name

e <- nqkeygen("ML-KEM-768")
kc <- nqkemcert(k$sk, "ML-DSA-44", cert, e$pk, "ML-KEM-768")
m <- nqsmimeencrypt(list(kc), "Content-Type: text/plain\r\n\r\nhi\r\n")
nqsmimedecrypt(e$sk, m, "ML-KEM-768")
```

## OpenPGP

`nqpgpkeygen()`, `nqpgpinfo()`, `nqpgpsign()`, `nqpgpverify()`, `nqpgpencrypt()`, `nqpgpdecrypt()`, `nqpgparmor()`, `nqpgpdearmor()`: `nqpgpkeygen()` makes a version 6 OpenPGP key (RFC 9580), by default ML-DSA-65 with Ed25519 and an encryption subkey of ML-KEM-768 with X25519, optionally under a passphrase; the others sign (a message that carries its data, a signature alone, or signed text), verify, encrypt to keys or to a passphrase, decrypt, and armor keys and messages as text. Only version 6 keys and messages are read.

```{r nqpgpkeygen}
k <- nqpgpkeygen("Ada Example <ada@example.org>", "ed25519")
nqpgpinfo(k$pub)$userid
s <- nqpgpsign(k$sec, "hello")
rawToChar(nqpgpverify(k$pub, s)$data)
e <- nqpgpencrypt("a secret", list(k$pub))
rawToChar(nqpgpdecrypt(e, k$sec)$data)
cat(substr(nqpgparmor("public key", k$pub), 1, 37))
```

## A store of other people's keys

`nqksadd()`, `nqkslist()`, `nqksget()`, `nqksdel()`, `nqkscertify()`, `nqksaddcert()`, `nqkstrust()`, `nqksexport()`, `nqksimport()`, `nqksurl()`: a key store is a folder that keeps public keys under names and addresses. A key is valid when a key the owner trusts has certified it: `nqkstrust()` sets how far a key's certifications count and `nqkscertify()` signs that a key belongs to its name. `nqksexport()` and `nqksimport()` carry a signature key with its identity card, and the keys it certified as its own, to another store; `nqksurl()` is the web address a key is published at for an e-mail address.

```{r nqksadd}
d <- file.path(tempdir(), "nqkeys")
dir.create(d)
me <- nqkeygen("ML-DSA-44")
bob <- nqkeygen("ML-KEM-768")
card <- nqidcard(me$sk, me$pk, "ML-DSA-44", "Me", email = "me@example.org")
mine <- nqksadd(d, me$pk, "ML-DSA-44", card = card)
his <- nqksadd(d, bob$pk, "ML-KEM-768", "Bob", "bob@example.org")
nqkstrust(d, mine, "ultimate")
cert <- nqkscertify(d, me$sk, me$pk, "ML-DSA-44", his)
nqkslist(d, "bob@example.org")$valid
nqksurl("bob@example.org")
unlink(d, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Keys on a token

`nqtoken()`, `nqtokens()`, `nqtokenlogin()`, `nqtokenkeys()`, `nqtokenkeygen()`, `nqtokenpub()`, `nqtokensign()`, `nqtokendecap()`, `nqtokenclose()`: these work with private keys that stay on a PKCS #11 token (a smart card, a hardware security module or a software token): the token makes the key, signs and decapsulates, and only the public key and the results leave it. `nqtoken()` takes the path of the token's PKCS #11 module. The example needs a token, so it is shown and not run.

```{r nqtoken, eval = FALSE}
t <- nqtoken("/usr/lib/softhsm/libsofthsm2.so")
nqtokenlogin(t, nqtokens(t)$slot[1], "1234")
k <- nqtokenkeygen(t, "ML-DSA-65", "release")
sig <- nqtokensign(t, k, charToRaw("a release"))
nqverify(nqtokenpub(t, k), charToRaw("a release"), sig, "ML-DSA-65")
nqtokenclose(t)
```
